nodes.label: Independent package tags (py-vX.Y.Z / web-vX.Y.Z)
nodes.rationale: Python and web packages are versioned independently; apps pin git tags only after validated releases.

nodes.label: Repository snapshot releases (vX.Y.Z) from Conventional Commits
Connect-time IP pinning
nodes.rationale: Fetcher validates every DNS answer and connects to the validated numeric IP while preserving TLS SNI and Host, preventing DNS rebinding SSRF.

nodes.label: 100% line and branch coverage for security modules
nodes.rationale: Coverage establishes regression coverage for fetching, sessions, privacy, log scrubbing, Redis admission, budgets, Turnstile; not a substitute for security review.

nodes.label: scripts/scan_secrets.py historical fixture allowlist
nodes.rationale: Recognizes exactly two fake URI fixtures in immutable commits instead of rewriting Git history or skipping detectors.

nodes.label: Semver version policy for v1+ packages
nodes.rationale: Patch for compatible fixes incl. stricter unsafe-input rejection; minor for additive exports; major for removed exports or changed shapes/settings formats.

nodes.label: Empty package initializers
nodes.rationale: Import the defining module, not the package root; underscore modules are internal.

nodes.label: ADR 001: Two independently versioned packages
nodes.rationale: Python and browser consumers upgrade at different rates; only primitives needed by both apps belong here.

nodes.label: ADR 002: Functions and explicit lifecycle ownership
nodes.rationale: Prefer functions/closures and typed data; caller-owned injected clients; no network at import time.

nodes.label: ADR 003: Atomic admission, conservative accounting
nodes.rationale: Redis Lua with server time and colocated hash-slot keys serializes caps across workers; fixed-point micro-units round up; fail closed.

nodes.label: ADR 004: Owner-bound progress, application-owned workers
nodes.rationale: Redis state plus trimmed streams supports snapshots/reconnects without choosing a queue framework.

nodes.label: ADR 005: Native controls and forgiving progress
nodes.rationale: Light DOM native controls let hosts theme without frameworks; timers start on intent; completed work survives pauses; no surprise motion.

nodes.label: ADR 006: Stable contracts require consumer evidence
nodes.rationale: Dev versions stay marked until real ClearRead and SoundSight integration passes.

nodes.label: Monotonic job status transitions
nodes.rationale: queued->running->terminal; terminal states final; stale regressions fail rather than erase earned progress.

nodes.label: Last-Event-ID replay with snapshots
nodes.rationale: At-least-once delivery; clients apply snapshots by sequence instead of incrementing counters.

nodes.label: Redis Lua scripts with shared cluster hash slot
nodes.rationale: Atomic script execution so all workers enforcing one cap serialize; keys share a hash slot.

nodes.label: Reservation receipt
nodes.rationale: Data, not a bearer credential; replay does not authorize paid work again.

nodes.label: Fail-closed on storage errors
nodes.rationale: StorageUnavailable must deny paid work, never fall back to an in-memory per-process counter.

nodes.label: Owner-controlled PyPI/npm publication
nodes.rationale: Publication requires owner approval and consumer acceptance; web private:true prevents accidental stable claims.

nodes.label: Phase E: jobs and web activities
Default log scrubbing
nodes.rationale: JSON handler drops bodies, headers, URLs, IPs, exception text to avoid leaking user data.

nodes.label: Five themes (light, dark, sepia, contrast, calm) and --ak- tokens
Bundled Atkinson Hyperlegible and Noto Sans fonts
Connect job progress via SSE to ak-progress
nodes.rationale: Apply snapshots directly, discard lower sequences, close EventSource on terminal events, use textContent for labels.

hyperedges.label: Job progress to browser via SSE
Forgiving progress and session activity components
